dutchForms.usageMeaning: present possession, availability, or a current state
dutchForms.commonUsage: Ik heb tijd. / Heb jij tijd?

canonicalExample.te: నాకు ఈ రోజు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.

commonUsageExample.en: Do you have time for coffee?

dutchForms.sentence: Ik heb vandaag genoeg tijd gehad.
dutchForms.naturalEnglish: I have had enough time today.
dutchForms.usageMeaning: a completed possession or experience viewed from the present

canonicalExample.nl: Ik heb vandaag genoeg tijd gehad.
canonicalExample.en: I have had enough time today.
canonicalExample.te: నాకు ఈ రోజు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.

dutchForms.usageMeaning: past possession, availability, or background state
a completed possession before another past reference point
dutchForms.commonUsage: Ik had al genoeg tijd gehad voordat de vergadering begon.

dutchForms.usageMeaning: an explicit future possession or prediction
dutchForms.commonUsage: Morgen heb ik tijd. / Ik zal morgen tijd hebben.

dutchForms.sentence: Ik zal de afspraak gehad hebben.
dutchForms.naturalEnglish: I will have had the appointment.
dutchForms.usageMeaning: a completed possession or experience before a future reference point

commonUsageExample.nl: Tegen vrijdag zal ik de afspraak gehad hebben.

dutchForms.sentence: Ik zou genoeg tijd gehad hebben.

dutchForms.usageMeaning: an unreal or unrealised completed possession

canonicalExample.en: I would have had enough time.

commonUsageExample.nl: Als ik eerder was begonnen, zou ik genoeg tijd gehad hebben.

englishComparison.situation: A present possession or available resource.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch uses the present form heb for possession and availability.

meaningPreserving.te: నాకు ఈ రోజు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.

everyday.te: నాకు ఈ రోజు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use OTT heb + a current-day cue.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch uses the present form heb for possession and availability.

englishComparison.english: I am having a difficult day.
englishComparison.situation: A current state described with an English continuous form.
englishComparison.meaningPreservingDutch: Ik heb vandaag een moeilijke dag.
englishComparison.commonEverydayDutch: Ik heb vandaag een moeilijke dag.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch normally uses OTT for a current state; it does not need a separate continuous tense here.

meaningPreserving.nl: Ik heb vandaag een moeilijke dag.
meaningPreserving.en: I am having a difficult day.

everyday.nl: Ik heb vandaag een moeilijke dag.
everyday.en: I am having a difficult day.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use OTT heb; vandaag supplies the current-period meaning.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch normally uses OTT for a current state; it does not need a separate continuous tense here.

englishComparison.english: I have had enough time this week.
englishComparison.situation: A completed or accumulated experience connected to the current period.
englishComparison.meaningPreservingDutch: Ik heb deze week genoeg tijd gehad.
englishComparison.commonEverydayDutch: Ik heb deze week genoeg tijd gehad.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: The lexical verb hebben uses gehad as its participle in this completed experience.

meaningPreserving.nl: Ik heb deze week genoeg tijd gehad.
meaningPreserving.te: ఈ వారం నాకు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.
meaningPreserving.en: I have had enough time this week.

everyday.nl: Ik heb deze week genoeg tijd gehad.
everyday.te: ఈ వారం నాకు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.
everyday.en: I have had enough time this week.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use VTT heb gehad + the current-period cue.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: The lexical verb hebben uses gehad as its participle in this completed experience.

englishComparison.english: I have been having trouble for days.
englishComparison.situation: A current problem continuing from an earlier point.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch commonly expresses the continuing state with OTT and a duration phrase rather than a separate continuous perfect.

meaningPreserving.en: I have been having trouble for days.

everyday.en: I have been having trouble for days.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use OTT heb + al + duration.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch commonly expresses the continuing state with OTT and a duration phrase rather than a separate continuous perfect.

englishComparison.situation: A past possession or available resource.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Had is the past singular form of hebben for a past state or possession.
englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use OVT had + a past-time cue.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Had is the past singular form of hebben for a past state or possession.

englishComparison.english: I was having a difficult day when you called.
englishComparison.situation: A past state in progress when another event happened.
englishComparison.meaningPreservingDutch: Ik had een moeilijke dag toen je belde.
englishComparison.commonEverydayDutch: Ik had een moeilijke dag toen je belde.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch normally uses OVT and context to express this ongoing past state.

meaningPreserving.nl: Ik had een moeilijke dag toen je belde.
meaningPreserving.te: నువ్వు ఫోన్ చేసినప్పుడు నాకు కష్టమైన రోజు.
meaningPreserving.en: I was having a difficult day when you called.

everyday.en: I was having a difficult day when you called.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Meaning-preserving: OVT had + the past reference. Everyday: OVT had when the surrounding context is already clear.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch normally uses OVT and context to express this ongoing past state.

englishComparison.english: I had already had enough time before the meeting.
englishComparison.situation: A completed possession before another past reference point.
englishComparison.meaningPreservingDutch: Ik had al genoeg tijd gehad voordat de vergadering begon.
englishComparison.commonEverydayDutch: Ik had al genoeg tijd gehad voordat de vergadering begon.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: VVT repeats had as auxiliary plus gehad as participle to place the completed state earlier in the past.

meaningPreserving.nl: Ik had al genoeg tijd gehad voordat de vergadering begon.
meaningPreserving.te: సమావేశం ప్రారంభమయ్యే ముందు నాకు ఇప్పటికే తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.
meaningPreserving.en: I had already had enough time before the meeting.

everyday.nl: Ik had al genoeg tijd gehad voordat de vergadering begon.
everyday.te: సమావేశం ప్రారంభమయ్యే ముందు నాకు ఇప్పటికే తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.
everyday.en: I had already had enough time before the meeting.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use VVT had gehad + al + voordat.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: VVT repeats had as auxiliary plus gehad as participle to place the completed state earlier in the past.

englishComparison.english: I had been having trouble for days.
englishComparison.situation: A continuing past problem measured up to a past point.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch normally uses had plus a duration phrase rather than a separate past-perfect-continuous tense.

meaningPreserving.en: I had been having trouble for days.

everyday.en: I had been having trouble for days.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Both roles use OVT had + al + duration.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch normally uses had plus a duration phrase rather than a separate past-perfect-continuous tense.

englishComparison.situation: A future possession or available resource.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch often uses OTT with a future time marker; zal hebben makes the future explicit.
englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Meaning-preserving: OTTT zal hebben. Everyday: OTT heb + the future-time cue.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch often uses OTT with a future time marker; zal hebben makes the future explicit.

englishComparison.english: At eight, I will be having dinner.
englishComparison.situation: A future activity expressed with an English continuous form.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch chooses the ordinary activity expression; having in English does not require Dutch zullen hebben.

meaningPreserving.nl: Om acht uur ben ik aan het eten.
meaningPreserving.te: ఎనిమిది గంటలకు నేను భోజనం చేస్తూ ఉంటాను.
meaningPreserving.en: At eight, I will be having dinner.

everyday.en: At eight, I will be having dinner.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Meaning-preserving: OTT aan het eten. Everyday: ordinary activity verb eet + the future-time cue.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: The English idiom having dinner maps to an activity verb in Dutch; Dutch does not require zullen hebben.

englishComparison.english: By Friday, I will have had the appointment.
englishComparison.situation: A completed possession or experience before a future deadline.
englishComparison.meaningPreservingDutch: Tegen vrijdag zal ik de afspraak gehad hebben.
englishComparison.commonEverydayDutch: Tegen vrijdag heb ik de afspraak gehad.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: VTTT makes the future reference explicit, while everyday Dutch may use VTT with the deadline phrase.

meaningPreserving.nl: Tegen vrijdag zal ik de afspraak gehad hebben.
meaningPreserving.te: శుక్రవారం నాటికి నాకు ఆ అపాయింట్‌మెంట్ అయి ఉంటుంది.
meaningPreserving.en: By Friday, I will have had the appointment.

everyday.nl: Tegen vrijdag heb ik de afspraak gehad.
everyday.te: శుక్రవారం నాటికి నాకు ఆ అపాయింట్‌మెంట్ అయి ఉంటుంది.
everyday.en: By Friday, I will have had the appointment.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Meaning-preserving: VTTT gehad hebben. Everyday: VTT gehad + the deadline.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: VTTT makes the future reference explicit, while everyday Dutch may use VTT with the deadline phrase.

englishComparison.english: By next month, I will have had this job for a year.
englishComparison.situation: A possession or situation continuing up to a future point.
englishComparison.meaningPreservingDutch: Volgende maand heb ik deze baan een jaar.
englishComparison.commonEverydayDutch: Volgende maand heb ik deze baan een jaar.
englishComparison.mismatchNote: Dutch uses a future time phrase and duration with OTT rather than a separate future-perfect-continuous form.

meaningPreserving.nl: Volgende maand zal ik deze baan een jaar hebben.
meaningPreserving.te: వచ్చే నెలకు నాకు ఈ ఉద్యోగం ఒక సంవత్సరం ఉంటుంది.
meaningPreserving.en: By next month, I will have had this job for a year.

everyday.nl: Volgende maand heb ik deze baan een jaar.
everyday.te: వచ్చే నెలకు నాకు ఈ ఉద్యోగం ఒక సంవత్సరం ఉంటుంది.
everyday.en: By next month, I will have had this job for a year.

englishComparison.howDutchExpressesIt: Meaning-preserving: OTTT zal hebben + duration. Everyday: OTT heb + future-time cue + duration.
englishComparison.whyTheyDiffer: Dutch uses a future time phrase and duration with OTT rather than a separate future-perfect-continuous form.

journeys.title: What I have and what is available
journeys.subtitle: OTT · possession and availability
journeys.learningGoal: Describe present possession, availability, and relationships with the correct present form of hebben.

story.nl: Ik heb vandaag genoeg tijd.
story.english: I have enough time today.
story.telugu: ఈ రోజు నాకు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.

story.nl: Mijn broer heeft een nieuwe fiets.
story.english: My brother has a new bicycle.
story.telugu: నా సోదరుడికి కొత్త సైకిల్ ఉంది.

story.nl: Heb jij een moment voor mij?
story.english: Do you have a moment for me?
story.telugu: నీకు నా కోసం ఒక క్షణం సమయం ఉందా?

story.nl: Wij hebben thuis een rustige plek.
story.english: We have a quiet place at home.
story.telugu: మాకు ఇంట్లో ఒక ప్రశాంతమైన స్థలం ఉంది.

story.nl: Ik heb alles voor de afspraak.
story.english: I have everything for the appointment.
story.telugu: అపాయింట్‌మెంట్ కోసం నా దగ్గర అన్నీ ఉన్నాయి.

notice.title: Who has what?
notice.subtitle: Notice how present hebben changes with the subject.

comparison.label: hij/zij
comparison.sentence: Mijn broer heeft een nieuwe fiets.
comparison.meaning: my brother has a new bicycle

comparison.label: wij
comparison.sentence: Wij hebben thuis een rustige plek.
comparison.meaning: we have a quiet place at home

notice.formula: ik heb · jij hebt · hij/zij heeft · wij hebben
notice.formulaNote: The present form changes with the subject. In a question, the finite verb can come first: Heb jij tijd?
notice.valuableContrast: Ik heb, jij hebt, hij heeft, and wij hebben all describe present possession or availability; the subject decides the form.

journeys.title: What I feel, need, and have time for
journeys.subtitle: OTT · common expressions and questions
journeys.learningGoal: Use common present hebben expressions and questions for feelings, needs, and available time.

story.nl: Ik heb honger na mijn werk.
story.english: I am hungry after my work.
story.telugu: నా పని తర్వాత నాకు ఆకలిగా ఉంది.

story.nl: Heb jij tijd voor een korte wandeling?
story.english: Do you have time for a short walk?
story.telugu: చిన్న నడకకు నీకు సమయం ఉందా?

story.nl: Mijn zus heeft zin in koffie.
story.english: My sister feels like having coffee.
story.telugu: నా సోదరికి కాఫీ తాగాలని ఉంది.

story.nl: Wij hebben vandaag weinig tijd.
story.english: We have little time today.
story.telugu: ఈ రోజు మాకు తక్కువ సమయం ఉంది.

story.nl: Ik heb geen last van de regen.
story.english: The rain does not bother me.
story.telugu: వర్షం వల్ల నాకు ఇబ్బంది లేదు.

notice.title: Present hebben expressions
notice.subtitle: Common feelings and needs use hebben in the present.

comparison.label: statement
comparison.sentence: Ik heb honger na mijn werk.

comparison.label: question
comparison.sentence: Heb jij tijd voor een korte wandeling?

comparison.label: third person
comparison.sentence: Mijn zus heeft zin in koffie.

notice.formula: ik heb · jij hebt · hij/zij heeft · wij hebben
notice.formulaNote: Fixed everyday expressions still use the subject's present form. In a question, Heb or Heeft comes before the subject.
notice.valuableContrast: Ik heb honger and Mijn zus heeft zin in koffie describe current states; Heb jij tijd? asks whether time is available now.

journeys.title: What I had
journeys.subtitle: OVT · past possession and background
journeys.learningGoal: Describe past possession, availability, and background states with had and hadden.

story.nl: Gisteren had ik meer tijd.
story.english: Yesterday I had more time.
story.telugu: నిన్న నాకు ఎక్కువ సమయం ఉంది.

story.nl: Vroeger had mijn vader een kleine winkel.
story.english: My father used to have a small shop.
story.telugu: గతంలో నా తండ్రికి ఒక చిన్న దుకాణం ఉండేది.

story.nl: Ik had toen geen fiets.
story.english: I did not have a bicycle then.
story.telugu: అప్పుడు నా దగ్గర సైకిల్ లేదు.

story.nl: Had jij vroeger een hond?
story.english: Did you use to have a dog?
story.telugu: గతంలో నీకు కుక్క ఉండేదా?

story.nl: We hadden thuis een grote tafel.
story.english: We had a large table at home.
story.telugu: మా ఇంట్లో ఒక పెద్ద బల్ల ఉండేది.

notice.title: Looking back with had
notice.subtitle: Had and hadden place possession or a state in the past.

comparison.label: past plural
comparison.sentence: We hadden thuis een grote tafel.

notice.formula: ik had · jij had · hij/zij had · wij hadden
notice.formulaNote: The past singular is had; the plural form is hadden. A question can begin with Had: Had jij vroeger een hond?
notice.valuableContrast: Gisteren had ik meer tijd looks back to a past state. We hadden uses the plural form, while present possession uses heb or hebben.

journeys.title: What I have had
journeys.subtitle: VTT · completed experience and states
journeys.learningGoal: Describe a completed experience or state with hebben gehad and distinguish it from present possession and past background.

story.nl: Ik heb vandaag genoeg tijd gehad.
story.english: I have had enough time today.
story.telugu: ఈ రోజు నాకు తగినంత సమయం ఉంది.

story.nl: We hebben samen een fijne dag gehad.
story.english: We have had a pleasant day together.
story.telugu: మేము కలిసి ఒక మంచి రోజును గడిపాము.

story.nl: Heeft zij ooit zo'n lange reis gehad?
story.english: Has she ever had such a long journey?
story.telugu: ఆమె ఎప్పుడైనా ఇంత పొడవైన ప్రయాణం చేసిందా?

story.nl: Ik heb een goede ervaring gehad met deze cursus.
story.english: I have had a good experience with this course.
story.telugu: ఈ కోర్సుతో నాకు మంచి అనుభవం ఉంది.

story.nl: Hij heeft vorige week een drukke dag gehad.
story.english: He had a busy day last week.
story.telugu: గత వారం అతనికి బిజీ రోజు ఉంది.

notice.title: Having had the experience
notice.subtitle: Hebben gehad links a completed experience or state to the present.

comparison.label: completed experience
comparison.sentence: Ik heb vandaag genoeg tijd gehad.
comparison.meaning: an experience completed in the current period

comparison.label: past background
comparison.meaning: a past state viewed as background

notice.formula: ik heb gehad · hij/zij heeft gehad · wij hebben gehad
notice.formulaNote: VTT uses present hebben plus the lexical participle gehad. The experience can be completed while the time period still matters now.
notice.valuableContrast: Ik heb tijd describes availability now. Ik heb tijd gehad reports a completed experience, while Ik had tijd looks back to a past state.

journeys.title: What I have done
journeys.subtitle: VTT · common auxiliary hebben
journeys.learningGoal: Recognise and construct common perfect phrases that use hebben as the auxiliary, with a practical contrast to selected zijn phrases.

story.nl: Ik heb vandaag gewerkt.
story.english: I have worked today.
story.telugu: నేను ఈ రోజు పని చేశాను.

story.nl: We hebben samen gekookt.
story.english: We have cooked together.
story.telugu: మేము కలిసి వంట చేశాము.

story.nl: Zij heeft een lange brief geschreven.
story.english: She has written a long letter.
story.telugu: ఆమె ఒక పొడవైన లేఖ రాసింది.

story.nl: Ik ben vroeg naar huis gegaan.
story.english: I went home early.
story.telugu: నేను త్వరగా ఇంటికి వెళ్లాను.

story.nl: Mijn broer heeft de deur geopend.
story.english: My brother has opened the door.
story.telugu: నా సోదరుడు తలుపు తెరిచాడు.

notice.title: Choosing the practical auxiliary
notice.subtitle: Many completed actions use hebben; selected movement or state changes can use zijn.

comparison.label: hebben auxiliary
comparison.sentence: Zij heeft een lange brief geschreven.
comparison.meaning: a completed action with a direct object

comparison.label: practical contrast
comparison.sentence: Ik ben vroeg naar huis gegaan.
comparison.meaning: a selected movement example using zijn

notice.formula: ik heb gewerkt · wij hebben gekookt · zij heeft geschreven
notice.formulaNote: This lesson uses a small high-frequency set. It shows the practical auxiliary choice without teaching every Dutch auxiliary rule or participle pattern.
notice.valuableContrast: Heb gewerkt and heeft geschreven use hebben for completed actions. Ben gegaan is a selected movement contrast using zijn; learners need the authored phrase, not a universal rule.

journeys.title: What I will and would have
journeys.subtitle: OTTT · OVTT · VTTT · VVTT · future and conditional reference
journeys.learningGoal: Distinguish future plans and conditional possibilities, then recognise advanced completed variants with zal hebben and zou hebben.

story.nl: Morgen zal ik meer tijd hebben.
story.english: Tomorrow I will have more time.
story.telugu: రేపు నాకు ఎక్కువ సమయం ఉంటుంది.

story.nl: Als ik vrij ben, zou ik meer tijd hebben.
story.english: If I were free, I would have more time.
story.telugu: నేను ఖాళీగా ఉంటే, నాకు ఎక్కువ సమయం ఉండేది.

story.nl: Tegen vrijdag zal ik de afspraak gehad hebben.
story.english: By Friday, I will have had the appointment.
story.telugu: శుక్రవారం నాటికి, నాకు ఆ అపాయింట్‌మెంట్ అయి ఉంటుంది.

story.nl: Als ik eerder was begonnen, zou ik genoeg tijd gehad hebben.
story.english: If I had started earlier, I would have had enough time.
story.telugu: నేను ముందుగా ప్రారంభించి ఉంటే, నాకు తగినంత సమయం ఉండేది.

story.nl: Volgende maand zal zij een nieuwe baan hebben.
story.english: Next month she will have a new job.
story.telugu: వచ్చే నెల ఆమెకు కొత్త ఉద్యోగం ఉంటుంది.

notice.title: Looking ahead with hebben
notice.subtitle: Zal and zou separate explicit future reference from conditional possibility; advanced perfect variants stay labelled.

comparison.label: future plan
comparison.sentence: Morgen zal ik meer tijd hebben.

comparison.label: conditional
comparison.sentence: Als ik vrij ben, zou ik meer tijd hebben.

comparison.label: future completion
comparison.sentence: Tegen vrijdag zal ik de afspraak gehad hebben.

comparison.label: conditional completion
comparison.sentence: Als ik eerder was begonnen, zou ik genoeg tijd gehad hebben.

notice.formula: zal hebben · zou hebben · zal gehad hebben · zou gehad hebben
notice.formulaNote: OTTT and OVTT are the main future or conditional contrast. VTTT and VVTT are advanced reference forms connected to the map; they are labelled for recognition, not taught as a beginner gate.
notice.valuableContrast: Zal hebben points to an explicit future. Zou hebben depends on a condition. Zal gehad hebben and zou gehad hebben add completion before that future or hypothetical reference point.
